title: Stability Breeds Instability
hook: Things have been good for a while. That's exactly when people start borrowing too much.
statement: Long calm stretches quietly encourage the debt and risk that eventually cause a crash.
explainer: When things stay calm, people treat safety like it's permanent and borrow more against it. Risk builds where you can't see it, until one shock snaps it all at once.
sop: List every fixed payment and debt you owe no matter what.
Measure the Cash Flow actually available to cover it.
Divide Debt by Cash Flow to get your Fragility.
Stress-test it against a big revenue drop.
Pay down debt or build cash while things are calm.
equation_example: 2,000,000 in Debt against 500,000 in yearly Cash Flow. 2,000,000 ÷ 500,000 = 4. Higher means more years of cash just to cover what you owe, so you're more fragile. Lower means you can take a hit without breaking.
question: Write down what happens to your business if revenue drops 30% next quarter.
closing_statement: Build resilience while nothing seems wrong.
caption:
Principle Nº 359: Stability Breeds Instability

Things have been good for a while. That's exactly when people start borrowing too much.

Long calm stretches quietly encourage the debt and risk that eventually cause a crash.
